paid_ads.title: Penrose Skin: "Wanna pull? You need this fragrance" dupe yapper (Penrose)
paid_ads.what: A man to camera: "Wanna pull fine shit like this, trust me you need to get this fragrance… it literally smells like [designer], the most identical fragrance… a lot more affordable… lasts a lot longer." 28 s.
paid_ads.how: Hook = desire outcome, product = dupe of the expensive thing, 2 advantages (price, longevity).

paid_ads.title: Penrose Skin: Talking-jar CGI rivalry ("You copied me! That's theft!")
paid_ads.what: A CGI designer-cologne bottle argues with the Penrose jar: "You copied me! That's theft!" / "Can't copyright a scent, babe… And I've got your exact same scent. Plus pheromones. For $220 less." 43 s.
paid_ads.how: Two animated product characters (luxury versus yours) argue; yours wins on price and an extra benefit.

paid_ads.title: Penrose Skin: "I stopped buying $400 colognes" price-anchor demo
paid_ads.what: Overlay: "I stopped buying $400 colognes… and started smelling like this", a red arrow pointing at the jar, "$ave for ONLY $XX". 15 s.
paid_ads.how: One overlay sentence of the switch, an arrow at the product, a price.

qa_checklist: Hook lands in the first 1.5 s (video) or is readable at thumbnail size (static / slide 1).
Removal test: delete the product from the script. If it still makes sense, rewrite so the product is the payoff.
Matches the reference structure (same beat order and length band) before any creative twist.
Uses only real product imagery for the product; AI is for backgrounds, characters or b-roll, and is disclosed where required.
Every claim is on the brand's approved-claims list (PDP); no invented stats, reviews, doctors or customers.
Captions burned in and inside the safe zone; sound-off still understandable.
One clear CTA that matches the landing page offer.
Three hook variants delivered for the same body (test hooks, not whole new ads).
Avoid: Do not name or show a specific competitor's brand in a way that implies something false about them; blur names.
Avoid: Every "how to tell" point must be true and checkable.
Avoid: Static version: warning notice ("Please check before purchasing") works too, as in the featured example.
inputs: BRAND (name, product, price, offer, audience, proof points, banned claims)
ASSETS (real product photos/video, logo, fonts, colors)
outputs: brands/<brand-slug>.md with 3 concepts in the output schema below
